column1: # AVX2 VEX.256 integer encoder oracle: Layer A, R-02, the register-bank forms, the CPU-feature
# reader and the ISA entry guard. Columns: tag <TAB> instruction (Intel syntax, ' ; ' between
# statements) <TAB> bytes (hex, x86-64) <TAB> source. Row order = the record order of
# encoder_table_driver.mind, which emits every row through the compiler's own emitter code.
# source=llvm-mc / llvm-mc=encoder: llvm-mc --triple=x86_64 assembles the instruction to exactly
#   these bytes (the harness re-assembles every such row).
# source=encoder/objdump: register forms; llvm-mc canonicalizes the commutative src1/src2, so the
#   oracle is objdump -D -b binary -m i386:x86-64 -M intel decoding the bytes to the instruction.
# R-02e rows (kinds 94-99): llvm-mc=encoder where llvm-mc keeps the operand order; vpmuludq /
# vpand / vpor rows with a<8, b=8 are encoder/objdump (llvm-mc swaps those commutative sources).
